judged_text: The template dispatch `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares raw input strings against stored attendee emails case-sensitively, so the wrong email class is chosen when the caller's casing differs from what was persisted. If the input "Foo@Bar.com" was normalized/persisted as "foo@bar.com" (or vice versa), a genuinely new guest receives the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests were added' notice without the full invite, and an existing attendee receives the fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail invite; the two branches deliver materially different emails based on string casing.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), the branch `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` uses a case-sensitive string comparison between `newGuests` (passed from the mutation input) and `attendee.email` (coming from persisted attendees via `formatCalEvent`). The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) on either side, so if casing differs between what the caller submitted and what is stored/formatted, the wrong template class can be selected, resulting in the wrong email type being sent.
